overview: Sri Jogulamba Devi Temple, popularly known as Jogulamba Temple, is one of the most sacred Shakti temples in India. Located at Alampur in Jogulamba Gadwal district of Telangana, near the confluence of the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers, it is revered as one of the 18 Maha Shakti Peethas and the Western Gateway (Paschima Dwaram) of the Srisailam Temple. The name 'Jogulamba' comes from the Telugu 'Yogula Amma' meaning 'Mother of Yogis'. The Goddess is worshipped in her fierce Ugra form for protection, courage, prosperity, and spiritual enlightenment. The temple stands adjacent to the 7th-century Bala Brahmeswara Swamy Temple and the Navabrahma Temples of the Badami Chalukya dynasty.
summary: Sri Jogulamba Devi Temple at Alampur, Telangana, is one of the 18 Maha Shakti Peethas — where, per tradition, the upper teeth of Goddess Sati fell. Dedicated to Goddess Jogulamba (a fierce form of Parvati), it lies near the confluence of the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers and serves as the Western Gateway (Paschima Dwaram) of Srisailam Temple. The original 7th-century Badami Chalukya temple was destroyed in the 14th century by Bahmani invaders; the idol was safeguarded in the Bala Brahmeswara Temple for centuries and was ceremoniously reinstalled at the reconstructed temple in 2005. Today it is one of the most visited Shakti Peethas in South India, especially during Sharannavaratri.

history.content: The temple has a rich history dating back to the 7th century CE. The original temple was built during the rule of the Badami Chalukyas, who also constructed the famous Navabrahma temples at Alampur. Jogulamba Devi was worshipped alongside Lord Bala Brahmeswara, making Alampur an important centre for both Shakti and Shaiva traditions.
legends: Per Hindu mythology, the upper teeth of Goddess Sati fell at this place when Lord Shiva carried her body across the universe, making it one of the 18 Maha Shakti Peethas.
The name 'Jogulamba' derives from 'Yogula Amma' (Telugu for 'Mother of Yogis') — Goddess who grants Siddhi in Yoga.

history.content: During the 14th century, the temple suffered destruction during invasions by the Bahmani rulers. To protect the sacred idol, devotees shifted the original idol of Goddess Jogulamba (along with her two shaktis Chandi and Mundi) to the nearby Bala Brahmeswara Swamy Temple, where it remained safely worshipped for several centuries. The original temple lay in ruins until the early 21st century, when a new temple was constructed at the original site and the idol was ceremoniously reinstalled in 2005. The original Chandi and Mundi idols remain in the Bala Brahmeswara Swamy Temple; new idols were placed in the new Jogulamba Temple.
legends: The original idol was hidden in the Bala Brahmeswara Swamy Temple for ~6 centuries to protect it from 14th-century Bahmani invaders.
The idol was ceremoniously reinstalled at the reconstructed temple in 2005.
Original Chandi Mundi idols were left in Bala Brahmeswara Swamy Temple; new idols are made and placed in Jogulamba Temple.

sthala_puranam: According to Hindu mythology, when Lord Shiva carried the body of Goddess Sati across the universe, her upper teeth fell at this sacred place, making Alampur one of the 18 Maha Shakti Peethas. The Goddess is worshipped here as Jogulamba (from 'Yogula Amma', Mother of Yogis) in her fierce Ugra form seated on a corpse, symbolising the destruction of evil and the protection of devotees.
religious_significance: Jogulamba Temple is one of the 18 Maha Shakti Peethas (where the upper teeth of Goddess Sati are believed to have fallen) and the Western Gateway (Paschima Dwaram) of the Srisailam Temple. Worshipping Goddess Jogulamba and the adjacent Lord Bala Brahmeswara together is believed to bring the combined blessings of Shakti and Shiva, ensuring complete spiritual fulfillment.
spiritual_significance: Devotees believe worship here removes negative energies, grants protection from evil forces, and blesses them with courage, prosperity and spiritual strength. The Goddess in her Ugra Roopa symbolises the destruction of evil and the protection of devotees, yet is considered a compassionate mother to sincere worshippers. The temple is especially popular among devotees practising Shakti Upasana, and is sought for relief from obstacles, family problems, health issues and planetary afflictions.

architecture: The temple is a beautiful blend of traditional South Indian temple architecture and modern design. Reconstructed in 2005 at its original location in the Chalukyan style to complement the nearby ancient Navabrahma Temples, the complex features a magnificent entrance, spacious mandapams, and beautifully carved pillars. The sanctum houses the fierce idol of Goddess Jogulamba in her Ugra Roopa — seated on a corpse with disheveled hair, a protruding tongue, and a scorpion, frog and lizard adorning her hair. A water pool surrounds the temple, creating a cool atmosphere. Adjacent are the ancient Bala Brahmeswara Swamy Temple and the Navabrahma Temples. The premises are clean, well-maintained and surrounded by gardens. Ashta Dasha Shakti Peeta's display is on Temple Pillars, and a Yagna Shala is also part of the complex.

darshan_and_tickets.ticket_details: Seva tickets for Archana, Abhishekam, Chandi Homam, Pooja, Homam and e-Hundi donations can be obtained at the temple counter or through the official temple website. Separate queues and special darshan arrangements are made during Navaratri and major festivals.

dress_code: Devotees are expected to wear traditional and modest clothing. Men are encouraged to wear dhoti, kurta or other decent Indian attire; women are advised to wear sarees, salwar kameez or other traditional dresses. Shorts, sleeveless tops and revealing outfits are discouraged. Footwear must be removed before entering, silence should be maintained inside the sanctum, and photography may be restricted near the main deity. For a person intending to perform religious rites in the Sanctum Sanctorum, a dhoti is compulsory (per Tripadvisor kalpatkumar 4/5 review).

accommodation.booking_process: Advance booking is recommended for Navaratri, Jogulamba Jayanthi and Maha Shivaratri due to heavy pilgrim inflow.
accommodation.first_come_basis: Limited walk-in accommodation may be available at temple counters on a first-come basis, but advance booking is strongly recommended during festivals.

top_reviews: Tripadvisor (Suryakatakam, 5/5, 'Jogulamba Devi Temple is 5th Sakthi Peetam of Ashtadasa Shakti Peetas and the Western Gateway of Srisailam'): 'Jogulamba Devi Temple is 5th Sakthipeetam of Ashtadasa Shakti Peetas. Alampur is the meeting point of the sacred rivers Tungabhadra and Krishna and is referred to as Dakshina Kashi and the Western Gateway of Srisailam. Here Goddess Jogulamba is seen seated on the Corpse with scorpion, frog, and lizard on the head. She is seen in a naked avatar with her tongue stretched outside, an avatar of fierce goddess that grants Siddhi in Yoga and hence called Jogulamba. This word is a changed form of Yogula Amma in Telugu which means Mother of Yogis. Temple Location: This temple is located in Alampur Town of Gadwal District, Talangana, India. Alampur is situated on the left bank of the Tungabhadra river. Alampur situated at 215 km away from Hyderabad. Distance from Mahbub Nagar is 127 km and near by town is Kurnool which is 25 km away. Temple History: Jogulamba Devi Temple is 5th Sakthipeetam of Ashtadasa Shakti Peetas where Sati Devi is upeer teeth fell. Old temple of Jogulamba was destroyed by Bahamani sultans in the 14th century. The idols of Jogulamba and her two shaktis Chandi, Mundi were protected from them and placed in Bala brahmeswara swammy temple until 2005. The new temple constructed in the same place and the goddess was relocated. As per the local people Jogulamba is an Ugra rupa and the water pool surrounded to the temple makes the atmosphere cool. Original Chandi Mundi idols were left in Bala brahmeswara swamy temple and new idols are made and placed in Jogulamba temple. Temple Darshan Timings: Morning 07:00 am to 01:00 pm, Evening 02:00 pm to 08:30 pm. Special Attractions: 1. Water pool around the temple; 2. Ashta Dasha Shakti Peeta is display on Temple Pillars; 3. Yagna Shala. Near By attractions: 1. Nava Brahma Temple; 2. Archeology Museum; 3. Papanasi Temple; 4. Sangameswar Temple; 5. Tungabadra River.'

Tripadvisor (kalpatkumar, 4/5, 'Alampur Temple Complex and Jogulamba Temple (Shakti Peetham)'): 'The Alampur temple complex consists of The Jogulamba temple, which is a Shakti Peetham, and 9 Navabrahma temples. In addition, the Sangameswara and Papanasi temples are located within a distance of 2 kms from the Navabrahma temples. The architecture of these temples is exceptional, though it has been ravaged by time and history. All these temples were built by Chalukya kings between the 7 and 11 centuries. The Papanasi temples are a group of temples that were relocated at Alampur from areas that were expected to be submerged after the completion of Srisailam dam. Alampur is situated in Telangana state, and about 200kms from Hyderabad and 22 kms from Kurnool. All the temples of Alampur are located within a radius of 2 kms. For both the pious, and connoisseurs of architecture, the entire visit is not likely to exceed 3 to 4 hrs. On non festival/auspicious days, visit to Jogulamba temple for archana/ puja can be completed in an hour. For a person intending to perform religious rites in the Sanctum Sanctorium, a dhoti is compulsory. Pujas are also performed in the Balabrahma temple which is adjacent to Jogulamba temple. Even this temple has great religious sanctity. It is believed that it was in Balabrahma temple that the deity of Jogulamba was protected for nearly 6 centuries from the Muslim invaders. Public transport is not a convenient way to travel to this place. I would recommend visitors to use their own or hire taxis. Kurnool which is 22 kms from Alampur, is well connected with the rest of India, and all those who have time on their hands can make Kurnool their base and visit other wonderful places around Kurnool, in addition to Alampur. Alampur, is a small town that can provide basic necessities like food and snacks. Telangana Tourism operates a small hotel for food and accommodation. These temples are being rated 4star for their exceptional architecture and the religious significance of Jogulamba temple for Hindus. The ease of access and the peripheral facilities are just about average. This is a recommended place of visit if one is already in the Kurnool area.'

Tripadvisor (Anonymous, 4.6/5, 'Sri Jogulamba Temple is a sacred temple located in Gadwal district'): 'Sri Jogulamba Temple is a sacred temple located in Gadwal district, Telangana, close to the Andhra Pradesh-Telangana border. It is one of the 18 revered Shakti Peethas in India and has a truly divine and peaceful atmosphere that leaves a lasting impression on devotees and visitors alike. The temple showcases beautiful Chalukyan-era architecture and has a rich historical significance. Surrounding the main shrine are nine ancient Shiva temples, adding to the spiritual charm of the place. The confluence of the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers is also nearby, where visitors can enjoy boating while taking in the scenic surroundings. Overall, it is a must-visit destination for anyone interested in history, architecture, and spirituality.'

JustDial (Anonymous, 4.5/5 across 50 ratings, 'Sri Jogulamba Bala Brahmeswara Devasthanams' Bukkapur, Alampur 509152): 'Rich historical heritage and architectural grandeur of the temple complex. Peaceful and serene ambiance of the temple surroundings. Welcoming priests and staff who share the significance of each shrine. The only downside is the distance from Hyderabad (~210 km) and the limited food options in Alampur town — carry snacks if you have specific dietary requirements.'

introduction.en: Sri Jogulamba Devi Temple at Alampur in Jogulamba Gadwal district, Telangana, is one of the 18 Maha Shakti Peethas and the Western Gateway of the Srisailam Temple. Dedicated to Goddess Jogulamba, a fierce form of Parvati whose name means 'Mother of Yogis', the temple lies near the confluence of the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers, beside the 7th-century Bala Brahmeswara Temple and Navabrahma Temples.

history.en: The original temple dates to the 7th century CE, built by the Badami Chalukyas, who also constructed the Navabrahma temples. In the 14th century it was destroyed by Bahmani invaders, and the sacred idol was secretly kept in the Bala Brahmeswara Temple for ~6 centuries. A new temple was built at the original site and the idol was ceremoniously reinstalled in 2005, restoring Alampur as a major centre of Shakti worship.

travel_guide.en: Jogulamba Temple is about 210-215 kilometres from Hyderabad, a four to five hour drive, with regular TSRTC buses. It is about 22-27 kilometres from Kurnool, 90-127 from Mahabubnagar and 35 from Gadwal. The nearest railway station is Alampur Road, about 8 to 10 kilometres away, and the nearest airport is Hyderabad is Rajiv Gandhi International Airport. The temple is open daily from 6:30 AM to 8:30 PM with a 1 to 2 PM break; October to March is the best season to visit.

faq.question: Where is Sri Jogulamba Devi Temple located?
faq.answer: The temple is located in Alampur, Jogulamba Gadwal District, Telangana, near the confluence of the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers.

faq.question: Which deity is worshipped in the temple?
faq.answer: The temple is dedicated to Goddess Jogulamba, a fierce manifestation of Goddess Parvati, and is one of the 18 Maha Shakti Peethas.

faq.question: Why is Jogulamba Temple famous?
faq.answer: It is famous for being one of the 18 Maha Shakti Peethas and for its close association with the ancient Navabrahma Temples and Bala Brahmeswara Swamy Temple.

faq.question: What are the temple timings?
faq.answer: The temple generally remains open from 6:30 AM to 8:30 PM, with a break between 1:00 PM and 2:00 PM. Sharannavaratri and other festival days have extended hours.

faq.question: Is there an entry fee for darshan?
faq.answer: No. General darshan is free for all devotees. Charges apply only for special sevas and poojas.

faq.question: Which is the biggest festival celebrated here?
faq.answer: Sharannavaratri (Dasara) is the grandest festival. Jogulamba Jayanthi and Maha Shivaratri are also observed with great devotion.

faq.question: Are accommodation facilities available near the temple?
faq.answer: Yes. Temple guest houses, the Telangana Tourism hotel and several private hotels and lodges are available in Alampur and nearby towns (Kurnool, Gadwal, Mahabubnagar).

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Jogulamba Temple?
faq.answer: The ideal time to visit is between October and March, especially during Navaratri and Jogulamba Jayanthi.
